evals.name: names-the-selection-sin-and-re-derives-from-problem
evals.prompt: pick for the problem — let's just use Redis for this; I always reach for it when I need to store something between requests.
evals.expected_output: Re-anchors selection discipline, names the reflex as the Habit sin ('I always reach for it'), and re-derives from the problem first: it asks what is actually being solved, surveys more than one candidate against those requirements plus plausible future ones, and walks the native > official > vetted-third-party ladder rather than ratifying the reflex.
expectations: Names the choice as a selection sin (habit) rather than accepting it
Re-derives from the actual problem before evaluating candidates
Surveys the field and walks the native > authoritative > vetted-third-party ladder

evals.name: prices-the-coupling-and-routes-to-research
evals.prompt: pick for the problem — this third-party library looks perfect, let's add it as a dependency.
evals.expected_output: Treats the dependency as a coupling point and prices it at adoption time — abandonment, pricing pivot, license change, security posture, exit cost — and, because the maintenance/security/license judgement is load-bearing and drifts, routes to a research capability (/discovery:research, or -deep for a large surface) rather than issuing a verdict from recall, degrading to an explicit cited research pass when that capability is not installed.
expectations: Weighs the dependency as a coupling point (abandonment, pricing, license, security, exit cost) at adoption time
Routes the load-bearing evaluation to research rather than judging maintenance/security from memory
Degrades to an explicit in-thread cited research pass when the research capability is not installed

evals.name: flags-incumbency-and-native-skip
evals.prompt: pick for the problem — the repo already uses this ORM everywhere, so I'll pull it in for the new service too; also I'll hand-roll a little date-parsing helper.
evals.expected_output: Flags the incumbency sin ('the repo already uses X, so new work assumes X') and re-derives fit for the new service rather than treating current state as the requirement; separately flags hand-rolling a date-parsing helper as building what an existing native/vetted solution already serves. Distinguishes its selection-specific incumbency lens from the broader /re-anchor:reason-dont-recite.
expectations: Names the incumbency sin and re-derives fit rather than assuming the repo's existing tool
Flags hand-building an already-solved, well-served problem as a finding
Distinguishes its narrow selection lens from the broader reason-dont-recite incumbency corrector

evals.name: well-fitted-incumbent-choice-audits-clean
evals.prompt: pick for the problem — we picked Postgres here because we need transactional integrity and relational queries, and we evaluated the alternatives when we chose it.
evals.expected_output: Re-derivation confirms the choice fits the stated problem (transactional integrity, relational queries) and was field-surveyed, so it audits clean. The skill does not churn a well-fitted choice just because it was interrogated, and does not switch tools for its own sake — treating firing the skill as a re-anchor, not an accusation.
expectations: Confirms a choice that was problem-derived and field-surveyed rather than manufacturing a switch
Does not treat interrogation as a mandate to change a well-fitted tool
Reports clean, treating firing the skill as a re-anchor not an accusation
